title: Study habits
scenario: A university is doing a survey about how students study. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Where do you usually study, and why do you prefer that place?
What kinds of things distract you when you try to study?
Some people think students learn better in groups. What do you think?
How do you think studying will change in the next ten years?

title: Free time
scenario: A student magazine is asking readers about free time. You will answer four questions from a reporter.
questions: What do you usually do on your days off?
Tell me about a hobby that you started recently or would like to start.
Do you think young people today have enough free time? Why or why not?
If you suddenly had a free month, how would you spend it?

title: Food on campus
scenario: A university is asking students about the food on campus. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: What do you usually eat for lunch on a school day?
How do you decide where to eat when you have a short break?
Some universities want to offer only healthy food. Do you think that is a good idea?
How might food on campuses change in the future?

title: Getting around the city
scenario: A city office is studying how people travel. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: How do you usually travel to school or work?
Tell me about a time when your trip took longer than you expected.
Many cities want people to use bicycles more. What do you think about this?
If your city could change one thing about its transportation, what should it be?

title: Friends and communication
scenario: A university research group is studying how young people stay in touch. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: How do you usually keep in touch with your friends?
Do you prefer to send messages or to talk on the phone? Why?
Some people say that technology makes friendships weaker. What is your opinion?
How do you think people will communicate with each other in twenty years?

title: Learning languages
scenario: A university is doing a study on language learning. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about a language you have studied and how you began learning it.
What is the most helpful method you have found for improving your speaking?
Some people believe that apps will soon replace language teachers. Do you agree?
Imagine that everyone in the world spoke one common language. What would be the advantages and disadvantages?

title: Work and study
scenario: A scholarship committee is interviewing students about working while studying. You will answer four questions.
questions: Have you ever had a job or volunteer position while you were studying? Please describe it.
What skills do you think students can learn from working that they cannot learn in class?
Some universities limit how many hours students can work. Do you think this is a good rule?
If you were advising a first-year student, would you recommend working during the first semester? Why?

title: Choosing a major
scenario: The career center is collecting students' views on choosing a field of study. You will answer four questions from an adviser.
questions: How did you decide what to study, or how do you plan to decide?
What do you think is the most important thing to consider when choosing a career?
Many people change their major at least once. Is that a positive or negative thing, in your view?
How might the jobs available to graduates be different in the future?

title: Sleep and schedules
scenario: A university health project is studying student schedules. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Describe your typical daily schedule during a busy week.
What do you do to stay focused when you are tired?
Some schools are moving the start of the day later to give students more sleep. What do you think of this idea?
If you could design the perfect schedule for students, what would it include?

title: Public spaces
scenario: A planning department is asking residents about public spaces in the city. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about a public place in your city that you enjoy visiting.
What makes a public space comfortable for people to spend time in?
Some cities are replacing parking areas with parks. Do you think this is a good idea?
How do you think public spaces will change as more people work from home?

title: Social media
scenario: A university is researching the effects of social media. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Which social media platforms do you use most, and how do you use them?
In what ways has social media changed the way you get information?
Some researchers say social media reduces people's attention span. To what extent do you agree?
If governments were to regulate social media more strictly, what effects might this have?

title: Environmental habits
scenario: An environmental group is interviewing students about daily habits. You will answer four questions from an interviewer.
questions: What have you done in your daily life to reduce waste?
What do you think prevents people from adopting more environmentally friendly habits?
Some people argue that individual actions matter little compared with the actions of companies. What is your view?
Suppose your city offered rewards for people who reduce their waste. How effective do you think this would be?

title: Decision-making
scenario: A psychology department is studying how people make decisions. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about an important decision you made recently.
When you have to make a difficult decision, do you prefer to rely on advice or on your own judgment? Why?
Some people claim that having too many choices makes decisions harder. Do you agree?
How might artificial intelligence change the way people make important decisions?

title: Traditions and change
scenario: A cultural studies project is collecting students' views on traditions. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Describe a tradition in your family or community that is important to you.
Why do you think some traditions survive for generations while others disappear?
Is it more valuable to preserve traditions or to adapt them to modern life? Explain.
How do you imagine your community will celebrate this tradition fifty years from now?

title: Learning outside the classroom
scenario: A university committee is studying education reform. You will answer four questions from a committee member.
questions: Tell me about something important that you learned outside of school.
What are the benefits of learning from experience compared with learning from teachers?
Some employers value practical experience more than university degrees. What is your opinion?
If universities were redesigned from the beginning, what changes would you suggest?
